title: Extrema of a Quartic W-shaped Curve
originalTopic: Finding all local extrema of a quartic
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A quartic like f(x) = x^4 - 4x^2 + 2 has three turning points, and a coarse window can make the middle one disappear. Locate all local maxima and local minima and state their values.

steps.title: Differentiate and factor
steps.explanation: The three critical numbers are 0 and approximately plus or minus 1.414, matching the W shape of the quartic.
steps.why: A degree-four polynomial has at most three turning points, so finding three critical numbers means none are missing.

steps.title: Classify with the second derivative
steps.explanation: The negative value at x = 0 makes it a local maximum; the positive values at x = plus or minus sqrt(2) make those local minima.
steps.why: Concavity decides the type of each turning point, which a picture alone can suggest but not guarantee.

steps.title: Evaluate the extrema
steps.explanation: The peak sits at (0, 2) and the two valleys at (sqrt(2), -2) and (-sqrt(2), -2), so a window such as [-2.5, 2.5] by [-3, 4] shows the complete W.
steps.why: The three extreme values determine the vertical span needed, and equal depths of the two valleys confirm the even symmetry of the quartic.
